post.description:
Verifies the supplied current password, hashes the new password
(bcrypt cost 12), clears the `mustChangePassword` flag, and writes
an audit entry. Used both for forced first-login password change and
for routine credential rotation from the profile page.

The only way to obtain a Bearer access token. Five failed attempts per
minute per IP are rate-limited; disabled accounts are rejected with 403;
every login is appended to the audit log. The `mustChangePassword` flag
signals that the user must hit POST /auth/change-password before reaching
any other route.
post.summary: Exchange credentials for an access/refresh pair

post.description:

get.description:
Returns the persisted `user` projection (never includes password hash
or refresh jti), the active tenant, and the resolved roles. Identity

user_roles × roles join — never from local state.

post.description:
Creates a new User with a temporary password and the
`mustChangePassword` flag, attaches them to the operator's tenant as a
tenant-scoped admin or member (super_admin assignment is forbidden via
this endpoint; the first super_admin is the tenant creator). When the
recipient logs in for the first time they are routed through
POST /auth/change-password.
post.summary: Tenant owner/admin creates a new member (admin or member)

post.description:
Rotating refresh: the old jti is revoked the moment a new pair is issued,
preventing replay. Refresh tokens are persisted jti-blacklisted so a
leaked token is invalidated on next observation.
post.summary: Rotate a refresh token into a new access/refresh pair

post.description:
Validates uniqueness of email, hashes the password (bcrypt cost 12), creates
the User row, opens a Tenant (Phase 1: `createTenant` defaults to true),
clones system role templates into tenant-scoped roles, grants the
`tenant.owner` role to the creator, seeds a `member_profile`, plants the
default automation rules, and issues the first access/refresh pair.
Five failed registrations per minute per IP are rate-limited (FR-005,
§3.3).

get.description:
Returns what the current session may do in personnel management:
which actions are allowed and which target roles are manageable.
admin receives member-only management; super_admin receives full
admin+member management; member receives none. The frontend must
derive route guards, menu entries and action buttons from this
response — never from localStorage or an identity switcher (FR-006,
FR-007). Server enforcement remains authoritative (FR-008).

get.summary: Server-derived capability set for the current principal

get.description:
Returns the fixed roles, the action catalog and the explicit
allow/deny grants evaluated by the authorization policy. The frontend
may cache it for rendering but must never treat it as the security
boundary; every mutating request is re-evaluated server-side (FR-006,
FR-008). Regression suites compare live behavior against this matrix
(FR-009).

Returns the three fixed roles super_admin, admin and member. The set
is closed: the API never admits custom roles, and unknown role values
are rejected everywhere they appear (FR-008). The frontend uses this
to render role labels instead of hardcoding its own copy (FR-007).

x-permission-matrix.boundary_decision:
admin may manage member only; super_admin manages admin and member.
This is the confirmed-safe default against horizontal privilege
escalation. Changing it is a contract change requiring matrix, tests,
and UI updates together.

invariants.statement: Any (action, actor, target) without an explicit allow rule is denied.
The final active super_admin cannot be disabled, deleted, or demoted by any flow.
role, status, or id values in request payloads can never widen the caller's scope; authorization uses the persisted target snapshot.
Unknown or missing roles are rejected at the schema and database layers.
Hiding a route, menu entry, or button is a UX projection only; the API re-evaluates this matrix on every request.
